The composite has a surface emissivity lower than 0.5 due to the Al-doped ZnO coating.
Thermal conductivity of the carbon nanotube-doped aerogel (CNTAs) is as low as 0.013 W/(m·K).
The polyimide (PI) fabric used has a fiber diameter of 10-15 μm and smooth surface morphology.
ZAO exhibits excellent thermal stability with almost no mass loss from 0 °C to 900 °C.
CNTAs show about 16.8% weight loss between 100 °C and 900 °C due to degradation of hydroxyl groups and CNTs.
PI fabric retains 53.8% char residue at 900 °C, indicating strong flame retardancy.
The limiting oxygen index (LOI) of the sandwich composite (ZAO/CNTAs/PI) is 29.7%, higher than PI fabric alone (26.6%).
XRD patterns confirm Al atoms substitute Zn sites in ZnO lattice without forming separate Al2O3 phases.
TEM images reveal CNTs embedded in the aerogel matrix, reinforcing mechanical strength.
The composite is prepared by hot pressing CNTAs on PI fabric at 180 °C for 120 seconds, followed by coating with ZAO.
The thermal conductivity model considering Knudsen effect estimates CNTAs conductivity at ~0.050 W/(m·K), close to measured values.
ZAO has high reflectivity in the infrared band (1000-10,000 nm), reflecting thermal radiation effectively.
The composite exhibits excellent flame retardant properties due to increased char formation and heat barrier effects.
Ansys Workbench simulations support the composite's superior thermal insulation and temperature distribution performance.
The sandwich composite material is lightweight, flexible, and suitable for advanced infrared stealth applications.
